Whiteboard academic web app: frontend handoff

Start with REPORT.html for the complete readable brief, or give Claude Code this folder and the prompt in START_HERE_FOR_CLAUDE.md. This package plans the web experience for students, instructors and teaching assistants. It is a specification and reference packet, not an implemented web app.

Prepared 4 November 2026 for the owner and their frontend developer. All sample institutions, people, grades and records are fictional.

What to build

First create an editable, offline HTML/CSS/JavaScript design prototype with coherent sample state and linked pages. Then the frontend developer can refine its appearance and port it to their chosen framework. Do not start backend, native apps, live integrations, deployment, paid AI or authentication services from this handoff.

The proposed catalogue contains 60 required web page templates, including the shared system-state template, plus 3 optional templates. This is a new academic planning inventory. It does not mean 60 completed features, and it does not replace or renumber the historical 50-destination/100-platform atlas. Dialogs, states and role variants are specified inside templates. Some templates can share an implementation component while keeping their distinct URLs and permissions.

“Required” means needed to complete this academic design brief. It is not a claim that all 60 pages belong in a first production release. Follow the staged build sequence and the page priorities.

Reading order

  1. spec/01_PRODUCT_AND_SCOPE.md: purpose, limits, product vocabulary and proposal status.
  2. spec/02_NAVIGATION_AND_PERMISSIONS.md: shells, route conventions and role authority.
  3. spec/03_SHARED_UI_AND_STATES.md: controls, design direction, responsive behavior and recovery.
  4. PAGE_CATALOGUE.md or data/pages.json: every page's fields, actions, validation, states, dialogs and acceptance checks.
  5. spec/04_WORKFLOWS_AND_RECORDS.md, data/fixtures.json and data/mock-service-contracts.json: connected behavior, concrete examples and later service-boundary shapes.
  6. spec/05_BUILD_AND_ACCEPTANCE.md: HTML-first sequence and review checklist.
  7. spec/06_DECISIONS_AND_TRACEABILITY.md: new proposed defaults, open decisions and all coworker feedback.
  8. research/: public evidence, dates and limits. This research supports requirements; it is not user testing or proof of demand.

Source hierarchy

For this new academic brief: owner instructions in the current engagement take priority, then the new specification and decision register, then page data and fixtures. Historical resources are references. Within this package, explicitly named cross-page rules override an accidental inconsistent page example; record and repair the discrepancy instead of inventing behavior. Do not silently resolve an open institutional policy question as a universal rule.

The original Whiteboard work accepted design direction and many workflows. New grading policy, groups, learner grades, TA calendar and other extensions here are proposed defaults for the developer's first HTML, not separately owner-accepted product policies. The owner has authorized this planning and packaging work. They have not approved every new requirement individually or authorized production implementation.

Included resources

  • A complete standalone HTML report, Markdown catalogue and machine-readable page specifications.
  • Fictional fixtures, workflow/journey inventory, permission table, proposed decisions and feedback traceability.
  • Original Whiteboard color/component CSS and selected academic source examples, with provenance.
  • The existing complete prototype as a historical reference. It contains wider campus roles; those are out of scope for the new build. It demonstrates older accepted designs and does not contain the newly specified missing workflows.
  • Local sample handout and submission SVG assets with text alternatives. They are fictional design fixtures.
  • Dependency-free build/verification tools and a SHA-256 inventory for this package.
  • FRONTEND_CHECKLIST.csv for the receiving developer's progress and VERIFICATION.md for the checks and limits of this delivery.

The coworker's original PDF, interview workbook, credentials, browser-local feedback, .git, caches and unrelated project folders are excluded. The feedback is normalized and traced in this packet; no private PDF upload was used for research.

Verify the delivered package

Extract the ZIP first. From the extracted folder, run python tools/verify_handoff.py (or py -3 tools/verify_handoff.py on Windows). It checks hashes, catalogue structure, IDs, source references, local links and fixture arithmetic. No dependencies or network are required. If Node is available, node tools/check_report.cjs exercises the report controller with DOM doubles. python tools/build_handoff.py --refresh-manifest rebuilds the report, catalogue, derived inventories and manifest after intentional edits; run the verifier again. Refreshing the manifest declares a new intended package state; verify the delivered ZIP before making edits.

Source/package checks do not establish browser accessibility or responsive usability. This package was not visually accepted in a browser. Review the future product HTML with the developer in a permitted browser, then record actual results separately from owner design approval.
